title: Secret: sensitive data in the cluster and the real limits of base64

videos.script: A Secret looks like a ConfigMap with a more serious name. That impression is closer to the truth than people expect. {{looks}} Its values are base64. Base64 is a way of writing bytes as text. It is not encryption, and one command undoes it. {{base64}} So what does a Secret actually protect? You will look for the password in three places: in the API, inside the pod, and in etcd itself, on the disk of the control plane. {{three}} In etcd you will find it in plain text. Then you will turn on encryption at rest, and look again. {{etcd}} The lesson ends with the protection that matters most every day: who is allowed to read a Secret at all. {{who}}
